patient.name: Douglas Harrington
patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait imbalance, sensory loss, and hand clumsiness over 3 months — worsening rapidly
patient.hpi: Douglas Harrington is a 66-year-old retired mechanical engineer and former 35 pack-year smoker who quit 12 years ago. He presents with a 3-month history of rapidly progressive sensory ataxia, gait imbalance, and bilateral hand clumsiness that has made him unable to write or button his shirt. His primary care physician performed initial NCS that reportedly showed 'neuropathy' and referred him to neurology for progressive gait difficulty. He describes the onset as bilateral hand and foot numbness occurring simultaneously — not the foot-first, length-dependent pattern he had heard about from a diabetic friend. He notes that his feet and hands feel like they belong to someone else, and he has near-daily falls at home. He has noticed his handwriting has deteriorated dramatically and he cannot perform fine motor tasks. He denies any significant weakness — he can rise from a chair and climb stairs — emphasizing that his problem is 'balance and feeling, not strength.' He denies bowel or bladder dysfunction. He does not have diabetes. He has lost 6 kg unintentionally over the past 4 months, which he initially attributed to reduced appetite. His wife notes he has been more forgetful over the past 6 weeks with occasional word-finding difficulty. He was treated empirically with IVIG 2 g/kg 6 weeks ago by an outside neurologist who suspected CIDP — he reports no improvement. He takes no medications known to cause neuropathy. He has no family history of neuropathy. He has no alcohol history. A chest X-ray obtained incidentally for a 'persistent cough' 5 months ago was read as 'within normal limits' but was not formally reviewed by pulmonology.
pmh: 35 pack-year smoking history, quit 12 years ago
Empirical IVIG 2 g/kg given 6 weeks ago — no clinical improvement
patient.review_of_systems: Positive: bilateral simultaneous hand and foot numbness (non-length-dependent), severe gait imbalance, falls, hand clumsiness, pseudoathetosis (unintentional hand writhing when eyes closed), unintentional 6 kg weight loss, persistent cough 5 months, mild word-finding difficulty. Negative: significant weakness, diplopia, dysphagia, bowel/bladder dysfunction, rash, joint swelling, fever.

medications.indication: neuropathic pain (started 8 weeks ago, minimal benefit)

family_history: Father: died at 74, colon cancer. Mother: died at 81, stroke. No family history of neuropathy, no pes cavus.

social_history.note: Retired mechanical engineer. Married. Former smoker 35 pack-years, quit 12 years ago. Non-drinker. No illicit drugs. No toxic occupational exposures. Lives at home with wife.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3 (disoriented to date). Mild word-finding difficulty on confrontational naming. Montreal Cognitive Assessment 24/30 (missed 3/5 words on delayed recall, 1 visuospatial task).
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No facial sensory loss. Mild saccadic pursuit eye movements bilaterally.
neurological_exam.motor: STRENGTH PRESERVED. Hip flexors 5/5, knee extensors 5/5, dorsiflexion 5/5. Upper extremities 5/5 throughout. No significant weakness. Motor power essentially intact — ataxia is sensory, not motor.
neurological_exam.sensory: SEVERE PAN-SENSORY LOSS NON-LENGTH-DEPENDENT. Pinprick: severely reduced all four limbs to mid-forearm and mid-thigh (NOT stocking-glove — involves proximal limbs and trunk). Vibration: ABSENT at all tested sites including knees and elbows (proximal level loss). Proprioception: ABSENT at toes AND fingers bilaterally. Joint position sense absent at ankles and wrists. Light touch: severely reduced all four limbs. Trunk: patchy reduced pinprick over thorax.
neurological_exam.reflexes: DIFFUSELY ABSENT. Achilles: absent bilaterally. Patellar: absent bilaterally. Biceps: absent bilaterally. Triceps: absent bilaterally. Diffuse areflexia with preserved strength — hallmark of sensory neuronopathy (dorsal root ganglion disease).
neurological_exam.coordination: SEVERELY IMPAIRED PROPRIOCEPTIVE ATAXIA. Finger-nose: dysmetric bilaterally due to sensory loss, not cerebellar tremor. Heel-shin: severely impaired. Cannot perform tandem walk. Pseudoathetosis present bilaterally at fingers when eyes closed.
neurological_exam.gait: Severely ataxic, wide-based, stomping gait. Requires bilateral arm support. Positive Romberg — falls immediately on eye closure. Unable to stand on one foot.
neurological_exam.special_tests: Pseudoathetosis: PRESENT bilaterally — involuntary writhing finger movements with eyes closed and arms outstretched (pathognomonic for severe proprioceptive loss from DRG disease). Lhermitte's sign: negative. No muscle tenderness.

output.interpretation: All sensory nerve action potentials absent bilaterally across 7 tested nerves. Motor NCS and EMG are within normal limits. The pattern of pan-sensory SNAP absence with preserved motor conduction and normal EMG indicates a sensory-predominant process at the level of the dorsal root ganglion or sensory neuron cell body, consistent with a sensory neuronopathy (ganglionopathy). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (8 WBC/uL) with mildly elevated protein (72 mg/dL) and normal glucose — a pattern consistent with inflammatory or immune-mediated CSF changes. Intrathecal oligoclonal IgG synthesis present (4 bands in CSF, absent in serum). Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) positive in CSF by immunofluorescence. No malignant cells on cytology. Clinical correlation recommended.

Abnormal: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) serum positive at 1:1000 (reference: negative; diagnostic threshold >1:240). Anti-Yo, anti-Ri, anti-SSA, and anti-SSB: negative. Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) is a paraneoplastic antibody found in a subset of patients with sensory neuronopathy and limbic encephalitis; a positive result warrants further evaluation for an underlying neoplasm. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.description: RIGHT HILAR MASS measuring 2.8 x 2.2 cm with irregular border. Central location adjacent to right main bronchus.
Multiple enlarged right paratracheal lymph nodes 0.8-1.4 cm.
Right adrenal nodule 1.1 cm — indeterminate on CT, PET needed to characterize.

additional_observations: Prior CXR was false-negative — hilar masses may be subtle on CXR
output.impression: 1. Right hilar mass measuring 2.8 x 2.2 cm with irregular borders, highly suspicious for primary pulmonary malignancy. 2. Multiple enlarged right paratracheal lymph nodes (stations 2R, 4R), 0.8–1.4 cm. 3. Right adrenal nodule 1.1 cm — indeterminate; further characterization recommended. No pleural effusion. No parenchymal nodules. Tissue diagnosis recommended.
recommended_actions: Further characterization of adrenal nodule recommended (PET or adrenal protocol CT).

findings: Bronchoscopy: right main bronchus extrinsic compression from hilar mass. EBUS-guided biopsy of right hilar mass and station 4R lymph node performed.
Pathology: SMALL CELL LUNG CARCINOMA (SCLC). Small cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin, nuclear molding. Ki-67 >80%. IHC: synaptophysin+, chromogranin+, CD56+, TTF-1+.
PET-CT: Right hilar mass SUVmax 18.4. Right adrenal nodule SUVmax 4.2 — ADRENAL METASTASIS (extensive stage). No osseous metastases.
Staging: EXTENSIVE STAGE SCLC (adrenal metastasis = M1b). TNM: cT2N2M1b.
output.impression: EBUS-guided biopsy of right hilar mass: small cell carcinoma. Immunohistochemistry: synaptophysin positive, chromogranin positive, CD56 positive, TTF-1 positive. Ki-67 >80%. PET-CT: right hilar mass SUVmax 18.4; right adrenal nodule SUVmax 4.2, consistent with adrenal metastasis. No osseous metastases identified. Staging: cT2N2M1b. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: anti-Hu paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy SCLC treatment prognosis

results.citation: Graus F et al. (2001) Ann Neurol 50:73-80.
results.summary: Anti-Hu present in 85-90% of paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy. SCLC in 80% of cases. Neurological symptoms precede tumor diagnosis in 60-80%. NCS shows pan-sensory SNAP loss with preserved motor NCS.

results.citation: Antoine JC et al. (2014) Neurology: Clinical Practice.
results.summary: IVIG is ineffective for paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy. Tumor treatment may stabilize but rarely improves neurological deficit. DRG neurons do not regenerate.

output.summary: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy is associated with small cell lung carcinoma in the large majority of cases. The electrodiagnostic hallmark is pan-sensory SNAP absence with preserved motor NCS, reflecting dorsal root ganglion cell body destruction. Evidence for immunotherapy (IVIG, plasma exchange) in intracellular-antigen paraneoplastic neurological syndromes is limited. Neurological outcomes are variable; extent of DRG loss influences recovery potential. Checkpoint inhibitor use in the setting of established paraneoplastic syndromes carries theoretical risk of neurological exacerbation; case series data are limited.

output.proposed: Carboplatin + etoposide + atezolizumab with gabapentin 300 mg TID, amlodipine 10 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg

interactions.description: Checkpoint inhibitors may WORSEN paraneoplastic neurological syndromes by amplifying anti-tumor immune response. Published cases of severe worsening of anti-Hu sensory neuronopathy with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. Risk-benefit discussion required — neurology co-management essential.
Both have renal elimination. Monitor renal function. Gabapentin dose adequate at current eGFR 82.

warnings: Checkpoint inhibitor use requires neurology co-management given established paraneoplastic syndrome

differential.key_features: CIDP presents with demyelinating NCS (slow velocities, conduction block) and responds to IVIG; this patient had IVIG failure. Pan-SNAP absence with completely normal motor NCS is DRG disease, not CIDP. CSF in CIDP shows albumino-cytologic dissociation without pleocytosis, unlike the lymphocytic pleocytosis here.

Sjögren's is the second most common cause of sensory neuronopathy; anti-SSA negative excludes it. No sicca symptoms (dry eyes/mouth). No salivary gland enlargement. Anti-SSA/SSB both negative in serum.

differential.diagnosis: Paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy from non-SCLC tumor
differential.key_features: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) at 1:1000 is associated with SCLC in 85-90% of cases. CT chest confirmed right hilar mass with pathology-proven SCLC. Anti-Yo (ovarian/breast) and anti-Ri negative.
No history of chemotherapy, neurotoxic medications, or high-dose B6 supplementation. Acute-subacute onset with weight loss and former smoker history points to paraneoplastic etiology.

key_reasoning_points: DIAGNOSTIC PUZZLE: The case was initially diagnosed as CIDP (elevated CSF protein + prior NCS 'neuropathy') and treated empirically with IVIG — the IVIG failure is a critical clue that this is not CIDP

CRITICAL NCS PATTERN: Pan-SNAP absence in all 7 tested nerves with COMPLETELY NORMAL motor NCS and EMG is pathognomonic for sensory neuronopathy (DRG disease), not CIDP (which shows demyelination) or axonal neuropathy (which preserves some SNAPs)
NON-LENGTH-DEPENDENT PATTERN: Upper and lower limbs equally affected simultaneously means DRG cell body destruction, not dying-back axon disease — this is the key localization clue
FORMER SMOKER + WEIGHT LOSS = SCLC UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE: 35 pack-year history with unintentional weight loss and anti-Hu positivity — chest imaging is mandatory even if prior CXR was 'normal'

PSEUDOATHETOSIS: Involuntary finger writhing with eyes closed is pathognomonic for severe proprioceptive loss from DRG disease — its presence indicates near-complete posterior column / DRG function loss

IVIG IS INEFFECTIVE FOR INTRACELLULAR ANTIGEN PNS: Anti-Hu targets an intracellular protein (HuD); antibody-mediated mechanisms are T-cell cytotoxic, not responsive to IVIG (contrast with NMDAR, LGI1 which do respond)
contraindicated_actions: Do not re-treat with IVIG when IVIG failed — ineffective for intracellular antigen paraneoplastic syndromes (anti-Hu, anti-Yo)
Do not trust normal CXR to exclude SCLC — hilar masses are frequently missed on CXR; CT chest is required in any former smoker with sensory neuronopathy
Do not start checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy (atezolizumab) without neurology co-management — may severely worsen anti-Hu paraneoplastic syndrome

red_herrings.data_point: Empirical IVIG treatment 6 weeks prior with no improvement — outside neurologist diagnosed CIDP
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors clinician toward confirming the CIDP diagnosis, potentially prompting repeat IVIG or IVIG dose increase rather than reconsidering the diagnosis entirely
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: IVIG failure is a critical diagnostic clue: CIDP responds to IVIG in 70-80% of cases. Failure after standard dosing should prompt reconsideration of diagnosis. The pan-SNAP absence with normal motor NCS is NOT CIDP — it is sensory neuronopathy (DRG disease), which is IVIG-refractory.

red_herrings.data_point: CSF protein elevation (72 mg/dL) with lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC 8/uL)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Elevated CSF protein could be misinterpreted as supporting CIDP diagnosis (albumino-cytologic dissociation); pleocytosis is not typical for CIDP and should actually argue against it
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: CIDP shows albumino-cytologic dissociation (high protein, NORMAL cell count). Lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC 8/uL) with oligoclonal bands indicates intrathecal immune activation from paraneoplastic CNS inflammation, NOT CIDP. Paraneoplastic CSF pattern: mild pleocytosis + elevated protein + oligoclonal bands + anti-Hu in CSF.

red_herrings.data_point: Chest X-ray reportedly 'within normal limits' 5 months ago
red_herrings.intended_effect: May provide false reassurance that pulmonary malignancy has been adequately excluded, leading to delay in CT chest
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: SCLC hilar masses are frequently missed or inapparent on CXR due to their central location and mediastinal overlap. CT chest is required for SCLC detection — CXR sensitivity for SCLC hilar masses is only 60-70%. A negative CXR does not exclude SCLC.
